Docket:

Introduction

[
1
]

Justin Rao is charged with several offences
arising out of an incident which took place in the early morning hours of
December 7, 2008 in Burnaby, British Columbia:

Count one:  Break and enter of a
dwelling house situated at 6513 Clinton Street, Burnaby, B.C. and commit an
indictable offence, sexual assault, contrary to
Section 348(1)
(d) of the
Criminal
Code

Count two:  Unlawful confinement of J.K.,
T-C, K., L.K. and A. K., contrary to
Section 279(2)
of the
Criminal Code

Count four: Sexual assault of L.K. as
a party with Jason Robert MacFadden, contrary to
Section 272(1)
(d) of the
Criminal
Code

Count five:
Robbery of J.K. and T-C. K., contrary to
Section 344(1)
(b) of the
Criminal
Code
.

[
2
]

The Crown alleges that four men entered a
residence at 6513 Clinton Street in Burnaby B.C., around 3:00 a.m. on December
7, 2008.  T-C.K., his son J., and his two nieces lived there.  All were present
in the house at the time of the entry.  The intruders confined the residents by
guarding them and restricting their movements, stole several items using
threats of violence, and three of them sexually assaulted one of the nieces,
L.K.

[
3
]

Only two accused appear on the indictment before
me:  Justin Rao and Jason MacFadden.  Jason MacFadden pleaded guilty to
breaking and entering and committing sexual assault on the first day of trial.

[
4
]

The accused Justin Rao called one witness, his
brother Daniel Vicky Rao, who, under the protection of s. 5 of the

Canada Evidence Act
and the
Charter,
testified that he was with the
group and it was he, not his brother Justin Rao, who participated in the sexual
assault of L.K.

[
5
]

At the commencement of the trial, counsel for
the R.C.M.P. sought a publication ban in respect of the identity of undercover
officers.  No evidence that might have been covered by such a ban was called at
trial.

Evidence for the Crown

T-C. K.

[
6
]

T-C. K. and his son J.K. lived on the upper floor
of 6513 Clinton Street in December of 2008.  T-C. K.’s two nieces had bedrooms
in the lower floor of the two-level house.  They had been living there for over
a year, and were preparing to move at the time of the offences.

[
7
]

Around 3:00 a.m. on December 7, 2008, T-C. K.
was awakened when someone opened his bedroom door.  He saw someone wearing a
hoodie, holding the side of it over his face, walk towards him and tell him not
to move.  The person was carrying a knife.  Since T-C. K. was facing the light,
that was all he could see.  The person told him not to resist, they only wanted
to take some things.  T-C. K. told him to take whatever he wanted but not to
hurt anyone.  The person took a notebook computer and a cell phone.

[
8
]

T-C. K. heard some commotion in the front of the
house and his son’s voice and asked if he son was okay.  His son said he was.
The man left the bedroom and T-C. K. followed him.  He saw his son sitting on
the sofa with a white man behind him telling him not to move.  He heard his
niece downstairs crying so he rushed downstairs.  The person with the knife was
with him, as well as the white man.  He could not see the person with the knife
very well, but he was not “a Canadian white guy” and not an Asian person.  He
was much taller than T-C.K., who is 170 cms.

[
9
]

When he got downstairs, the person with the
knife pushed him onto a sofa and his son was brought there as well.  T-C. K.
could see the same two people who had been upstairs.

[
10
]

He heard his older niece crying and vomiting.
He called to her asking what had happened but she did not answer.  He could
hear the sound of her being hit and crying.  The man with the knife went back
to that area.  T-C. K. took a pair of scissors and rushed forward, but the man
with the knife came back and said “do you want to be hurt?” and told him to
drop the scissors.  His son told him not to resist.  The person with the knife
told the white man to watch them and went back towards the bedroom.

[
11
]

The white male took a bottle from the kitchen
and held it in his hand, which T-C. K. thought was just to have something in
his hand because he did not have a weapon.  This man was not much taller than
T-C. K.

[
12
]

T-C. K. heard a male voice telling his niece to
“suck”, and the sound of her crying and vomiting.  He thought she was being
forced to have oral sex.

[
13
]

T-C. K. rushed towards his niece’s room several

the white man who never left the room.

[
14
]

Another man, dark skinned, came out of his
niece’s room, wielding his arms and kicking out with his legs, asking if T-C.
K. wanted to fight him.  He was about the same height as the man with the
bottle.

[
15
]

The white guy told them to leave quickly and they
left by the back door.  Although he saw only three people - the man with the
knife, the white male, and the dark skinned male who came out of the bedroom -
T-C. K. believes there was another man because other items were missing from
the upstairs when he checked later.

[
16
]

He said he saw only one dark skinned male.

J.K.

[
17
]

J.K., 24, who was still up working on his

intruders had not seen his new cell and he hid it.

[
18
]

He was told to go into the living room.  He went
to the living room and his father joined him.  The dark skinned man told

and T-C. K. followed them.  J.K. did not want to leave his father alone so he
followed as well.

[
19
]

When they got downstairs, he and his father

He pulled his father to the sofa.  Someone else, a Caucasian male, picked up a

[
20
]

He heard voices talking to his older cousin and

[
21
]

Because of a jog in the halls, he could not see

He was pretty sure he saw one of the men go back upstairs and not come down.
There is a back door upstairs that leads outside as well.

[
22
]

At some point, the person who had opened his
door upstairs, that is, the dark skinned man, tried to punch him when he pulled

[
23
]

He saw only one dark skinned male.  One of the

cannot be sure.

[
24
]

After awhile it got silent and he went back to
check.  The intruders were gone.  He went to the younger niece’s room and used
her cell phone to call the police.

The Younger Niece, A.K.

[
25
]

The younger niece was 18 at the time of these
events.  She was sleeping and was awakened by a man who opened and closed her
door quickly.  She did not get a good look at him.  The man had a mask on and

[
26
]

Another man opened the door, stayed outside the

[
27
]

She heard other people going to her sister’s
room.  She saw someone with her sister’s laptop and camera.

[
28
]

Then a dark skinned man came to her room, showed

[
29
]

She heard them say they wanted to go.  They

They left and a few seconds later the guy who said “wait” left as well.

[
30
]

The younger niece saw three men, but heard

living room.  She saw only one black man.

[
31
]

She sat and waited until she was sure only her
family was there.  Her cousin J.K. came to her room and used her cell phone to

The Older Niece, L.K.

[
32
]

The older niece, 24 at the time of the events,
testified only briefly.  She described the men coming into her room but was
unable to continue with her evidence.  After a
voir dire
, I allowed her
videotaped statement to the police, given several hours later, to be admitted
for its truth on a threshold basis.

[
33
]

In that statement, the complainant said she was

[

[

[

[

The complainant said a fourth man came in, said

[

]

[
46
]

In her brief cross-examination at trial, during

[
47
]

She said she helped the police with a sketch of
the only dark skinned man that she saw.

First Police on Scene

[
48
]

The police officers found L.K. to be shaking and
crying, not able to speak clearly.  She had a swollen lip, scratch marks on her
face, red marks on her wrists and a bruised jaw.

[
49
]

The police noted that there was a ladder up
against the front window, with pry marks on the frame of that window and also
on the frame of a lower window, a Smirnoff Ice bottle outside the bedrooms,
black leather gloves on the asphalt three or four houses away, and new dollar
store gloves with a 7-11 price tag on them on the other side of the fence from
the residence.  They also found a green and black jacket about a block away.
There was a pair of gloves in the pocket, similar to those found over the
fence, with a 7-11 price tag attached.

Sandra Stewart

[
50
]

The house where the accused Justin Rao lived
with his parents was across the alley from the Clinton Street address.  Sandra
Stewart, a neighbour who knew the Rao family well, said the Raos had been her
neighbours for twenty years.

[
51
]

She said she saw Justin Rao in the alley at
around 1:30 a.m. that evening.  Although usually friendly, he ducked into his
yard and did not acknowledge her.  He was wearing a hoodie and jeans and looked
scruffy and unshaven, which was unusual.

[
52
]

She was driving a friend home shortly thereafter
and saw other men moving furtively around the neighbourhood.   Still later, she
heard the Rao’s dog barking uncontrollably for some time and someone running past
her house.

[
53
]

She testified that a few days after the event,
Justin Rao came over to her yard to talk to her, and he had shaved off most of
his hair and his goatee and looked very much like his brother Daniel.

Videotaped Evidence

[
54
]

Videotapes were seized from surveillance cameras
in a nearby 7-11 on Royal Oak Avenue in Burnaby, about five minutes from the
Clinton Street house, and also from a liquor store across the street from the
7-11.

[
55
]

The camera in the liquor store camera is aimed
down from the ceiling at the door.  Jason MacFadden can be seen entering the
liquor store at about 7:20 p.m. on December 6, 2008, with another man who is
wearing a baseball cap which partially obscures his face.  The second man is
wearing a blue puffy jacket, knee length shorts and running shoes.  The youth
service worker for the Burnaby school district identified Jason MacFadden as
the first man and the second man as Justin Rao.  He said MacFadden and Justin
Rao were friends in school and hung out with the same group.  He said he knew
both of them very well.  A police liaison officer who worked at the school also
identified Jason MacFadden.  He thought the other male looked like Justin Rao
based on the description and the jacket but could not say for sure.  He agreed that
male could also be Justin Rao’s older brother Daniel Rao who looks very
similar.

[
56
]

Jason MacFadden, Brendan Roshinski, Jamie Sabbe
and some other young people are seen in the 7-11 just before 3:00 a.m., buying
gloves and apparently stealing items from the area where the condoms and gloves
are located.  Brendan Roshinski, who is tall with blond hair, is seen wearing a
green and black jacket that was found discarded near the Clinton Street
residence, and tested for DNA.  It had Brendan Roshinski’s DNA on it.  In both
videos, Jason MacFadden wears a dark jacket with a heavy grey stripe down the
sleeves.

Text Messages and Phone Calls

[
57
]

Text messages and phone calls were exchanged
regularly between MacFadden and a number which, although not registered to
Justin Rao, shows up on texts to a “Justin”, on December 6 and 7, 2008, both
before and after the incident, but not during, that is between 3:00 and 3:30
a.m.

[
58
]

The phone was registered to a person named
Sigouin Kyle, with user Valerie Kyle.  There was no further evidence about the
registered owner or user.

Medical Evidence

[
59
]

The complainant was examined at the hospital.  She
had injuries to her face, collarbone area, arms, thighs and knees.  The doctor
who examined her testified that the bruises to her thighs and knees were
consistent with someone using their fingers or hands to hold someone’s legs
apart.

[
60
]

DNA was obtained from nail clippings and from
many swabs from her body and items in the room.  Jason MacFadden’s DNA was
found on many items, including the vaginal and cervical swabs.  Justin Rao’s
DNA was found in one of the nail clippings.

[
61
]

The doctor who supervised the taking of the nail
clippings said the clippers come from the sexual assault service supplies and
are not in the sterile kit.  She said she cannot say whether the clippers were
sterile, but as far as she is aware the clippers do not come from a sterile
package.  She said there is a protocol to preparing the room but she is not
involved in it, so she could not say how and when the clippers were cleaned.

Evidence Obtained Through Surveillance

[
62
]

Daniel Vicky Rao, Justin’s older brother, was
observed to drop off some clothes at a dry cleaner’s the next day.  The clothes
had a tag with the name “Jay” on it and the phone number which was connected to
Justin Rao through the seizure of text records from Telus.

[
63
]

Daniel Vicky Rao also dropped off a bag of
clothes in a deposit bin the next day.  The clothes were seized and tested for
DNA.

[
64
]

Both Justin Rao’s and the complainant L.K.’s DNA
profiles were found on the interior crotch area of a pair of boxer shorts from
the bag from the deposit bin, which also contained a t-shirt, sweat pants and a
sock.  There was also trace DNA on the boxer shorts which was insufficient to
develop a profile.  From what was available, Daniel Vicky Rao and Danny Rao,
the third brother, could not be excluded from the trace DNA.

DNA Evidence

[
65
]

Many witnesses were called to deal with
continuity in respect of the DNA evidence.  The officers who dealt with the
seized clothing, took it to the lab, and each of the lab personnel who dealt
with those exhibits were called.

[
66
]

Of importance to the defence is the
acknowledgment by Cpl. Dosanjh that the clothing seized from the deposit bin
was all together in the plastic bag.  As well, Cpl. Dosanjh could not say if
she took the usual precautions of putting on clean gloves for each item when
she placed them into separate paper bags on December 9, 2008 and put them in
the exhibit room.  She could not say if she dealt with the t-shirt or the
boxers first.  Cst. Lopetinski, who was with Cpl. Dosanjh when she opened the
bag, said they were not concerned about cross-contamination because the
clothing was all rolled together in the bag in any event.  Thus the pair of boxer
shorts in the bag, which contained the DNA of Justin Rao and L.K. on the
interior crotch, was in contact with other items, including the t-shirt, which
had Justin Rao’s DNA on it.

[
67
]

Tanya Dare, the analyst, agreed on
cross-examination that if clothes are jumbled together in a bag, DNA could be
transferred from one piece of clothing to another.

[
68
]

She said the DNA on the crotch area matched
Justin Rao’s DNA and had been extracted from semen.  L.K.’s DNA was also
present.  She could not exclude either of the other Rao brothers from the trace
components that were present, although they did not match the semen component.
A trace component is DNA that is detected in a profile but the quality is so
weak that its statistical significance cannot be determined.  Ms. Dare
could not say that either of the other Rao brothers’ DNA was there, and she
could not say it wasn’t.

[
69
]

DNA on the t-shirt matched Justin Rao’s profile,
and she could not exclude Daniel Vicky Rao or Danny Rao from certain samples.

[
70
]

Ms. Dare said if she were told the nail clippers
used to obtain L.K.’s nail clippings were not sterile, it would open the
possibility for a DNA profile matching Justin Rao’s to have come from the
clippers themselves rather than the nail clipping.  Either Mr. Rao
contacted the clippers, or someone having contact with Justin Rao came in
contact with the clippers.

[
71
]

Ms. Dare said she concluded that neither of
the other Rao brothers’ DNA was in the nail clipping sample.  The brothers
share certain genetic characteristics, and on some of the tested items, she said
that she could not exclude Daniel Vicky Rao.  However on the nail clippings,
she compared Daniel Vicky’s Rao’s DNA profile and it did not match.  Even if
his DNA were in the mix, there was no doubt the major contributor was Justin
Rao.

Defence Evidence

[
72
]

[
73
]

Canada Evidence
Act.
Also under the protection of s. 13 of the

There is no doubt, on a consideration of all the evidence, that the

a common intention, broke and entered the residence at 6513 Clinton Street in
Burnaby on December 7, 2008, and committed robbery of T-C.K. and J.K.  Laptops,
cell phones and money were taken from T-C. K. and J.K., using threats of
violence.  Some items were also taken from L.K.  As well, there is no doubt the
members of the group unlawfully confined the residents.

[

]

There is also no doubt that L.K. was sexually assaulted by at least
two men, and on her statement, there were three.  The issue is what part Justin
Rao played in these events.  No one identified Justin Rao in court, with the
exception of one officer from the surveillance team who had obtained cast-off

the prisoner’s dock as Daniel Vicky Rao.

[

]

The defence says, based on Daniel Vicky Rao’s evidence, that Justin
Rao was there and took part in the break-in, unlawful confinement, and robbery,
but played no part in the sexual assault of L.K., except to try to stop it.
The Crown says Daniel Vicky Rao’s evidence should be rejected in its entirety:
he was not there and is lying to protect his brother.

R. v W.D.
,

, [1991] 1 S.C.R. 742:

- I must acquit the accused if I believe
Daniel Vicky Rao

- I must acquit even if I don’t believe Daniel

- Even if I am
not left with a reasonable doubt by his evidence, I must consider whether the
Crown has established its case beyond a reasonable doubt on evidence that I do

]
